title: Group-scheme linearization and geometric stability with full stabilizers
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme], $X$ a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an algebraic left $G$-action $a$, and $L$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A linearization consists, on every test $k$-scheme $T$, of $\mathcal O_T$-linear isomorphisms $x^*L\simeq(gx)^*L$ for $g:T\to G$ and $x:T\to X$. These satisfy the identity and multiplication cocycles and naturality under every test morphism, using the canonical pullback comparisons [def-pc-module-pullback]. Extend to powers by the canonical tensor-power comparisons already used in [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization]. A section of $L^{\otimes d}$ is invariant when its two pullbacks agree under those isomorphisms for every test scheme. For an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] and an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, a geometric point is semistable when some positive-degree invariant section is nonzero there. It is stable when it is semistable, its orbit is closed in the semistable locus of $X_\Omega=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and its scheme-theoretic stabilizer has Krull dimension zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The stabilizer is the equalizer, on $G\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, of the orbit map and the constant map at the point; no reduction is taken. For finite-type $G$ and $X$, orbit closedness is expressed by a closed subset of $X_\Omega$ whose semistable $\Omega$-points are exactly the orbit. Scheme, coefficient and test objects all use a fixed universe $u$.

source.place: Morrison, arXiv:0810.2340, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5, linearization as a lift to the total line; test-scheme cocycles and full-stabilizer stability are the explicit definitions used in the Hilbert-Pluecker node.
